chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever eats from this food, let him not enter our mosque.' He meant garlic, and he did not say that it is forbidden.
ai.seo_question: Is eating garlic forbidden in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies that the prohibition on entering the mosque after eating garlic is a matter of etiquette (adab) due to the strong odor, rather than a ritual impurity (najis) or absolute prohibition (haram). It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the permissibility of consumption and the social consideration required in communal worship spaces.
